_comment: Frozen message-format constants: the single source of truth both the FastAPI
backend (fastapi-backend/app/services/message_format.py) and the CLI's own copy
copy exists because the thin uv-tool CLI cannot import the backend.
Both test suites read THIS file and assert their own primitives against it, so
the two copies cannot silently drift apart (a drift -> a reply the hub can't
parse, or a room message read as a thread's). If a change to the shared shape
is genuinely intended, update this file deliberately in the same PR and both
suites will re-lock to the new value.

valid_subkinds._comment: Kind -> allowed subkinds. Backend: app.services.message_format.VALID_SUBKINDS (keyed by the Kind enum). CLI: mycelium.message_format.VALID_SUBKINDS (keyed by the plain string). An empty/None subkind is always valid for any kind. The exchange move subkinds counter/accept/reject are the closed negotiation-move vocabulary a coordination reply carries on the wire (counter = any offer incl. the opening one; accept/reject respond to the standing offer); team-formation predates them. ``amend`` revises an earlier message: parents carries the amended message's id, the payload carries the new text, and the read path folds the chain to the newest text. ``reaction`` puts an emoji on an earlier message or takes it off: parents carries that message's id, the content carries reaction {emoji, on}, and the read path folds it into that message.

ping._comment: The payload type a thread's activity surfaces into the room as. The backend PRODUCES it (room_channels.raise_ping, off app.services.message_format.PING_PAYLOAD_TYPE) on every write into a thread; the CLI READS it (mycelium.message_format.ping_of) to draw the one activity line `room watch` shows when a task moves. A ping deliberately carries no prose — only which thread moved, who wrote it and the message id — so payload_fields is the whole of it, and a reader expecting text would draw an empty line instead of the argument the thread exists to absorb. It is also what the backend's participate._addressed_to excludes, so a resident agent consumes a ping silently rather than spending a turn on it: rename the type on one side only and every agent in the room wakes on every thread write. The GUI is the third reader (mycelium-frontend/src/lib/threads.ts, ping_of + PING_PAYLOAD_TYPE): it draws the coalesced 'activity in <task>' notice the room sees in place of the thread's prose, so a drift here empties the channel of any sign its threads moved.

notice._comment: The payload type the room's board events surface into its timeline as. Where a ping says a thread moved, a notice says the board did: a task filed, claimed, handed back or resolved. The backend PRODUCES it (room_channels.raise_notice, off app.services.message_format.NOTICE_PAYLOAD_TYPE) at each seam — leases.claim/release/resolve, the memory upsert on a board-row create, and the lease sweep (lease_sweep.py) when a held lease drains past its TTL (`expired`, raised once per lease); the GUI READS it (mycelium-frontend/src/lib/threads.ts, notice_of + NOTICE_PAYLOAD_TYPE) to draw the 'New task'/'Claimed'/'Resolved' line the channel shows in sequence with the chat. Like a ping it is excluded from participate._addressed_to, so a resident agent consumes a notice silently rather than waking on it, unless it subscribed to that notice (app/services/subscriptions.py: a notice kind, or a task the notice is about): rename the type on one side and either the timeline goes quiet or every agent wakes on every board write. `data.subkind` is one of `subkinds` (a closed set); `data` always carries `subkind` and `key`, and a `filed` notice also carries the board `kind` so the line reads 'New decision' not always 'New task'. `floor` is the one notice about a thread rather than a task: raised by room_channels.hold_floor/release_floor when whose turn it is changes, with `key` the thread's short id, `by` the holder, `speakers` the comma-joined handles given the floor (absent when the holder alone has it) and `released` set when it opens back up. `upstream` says the external thing a row points at changed (a pull request's review or CI moved, or it merged or closed): raised by the status watcher (app/services/status/watch.py) when a provider's answer for a linked ref differs from the room's last one (or, for `opened`, when a ref is first seen open), with `change` one of `upstream_changes`, `ref` the provider's id for it (`owner/repo#123`), `url`, `label` the provider's own word for its state now, and `at` when the source changed. Nobody writes it and it wakes nobody but an agent subscribed to it (`upstream:<change>`, or the row's task): the wake digest lists it on the `Board:` line of whoever holds, was given or filed the row (a merge to everyone), and nothing else raises a wake for it. `quiet` says a held row has had no activity for a few hours, once per hold: raised by the hold sweep (app/services/hold_sweep.py) with `why` saying how long and who holds it. It is how the hub says a task went quiet without posting in the thread or waking anyone, and a row whose pull request waits on a review or a merge, or that names a blocker, never gets one. `check` is the one notice about a message rather than a task: raised by the verifier (app/services/verifier.py) when it finds a multi-agent failure in an agent's message (so far, a claim about an approval or a merge that the room's records don't back), with `message_id` the message it goes under (the `id` the room's history read gives it, as an upload's `posted_in` does), `envelope_id` the same message's envelope id (the `id` a live bus frame carries, so a client can find a message that arrived live before it reloads history), `flag_id`, `about` the agent that said it, `failure` which multi-agent failure it is (`ungranted_approval`, `stale_state`, … as app/services/verifier_records.FAILURES names them), `line` the sentence to show, `sure` ("true" when the records say the opposite, "false" when nothing was found), `quotes` the exact words to underline joined with U+001F, `ref` the pull request (`#1278`), and `state` (`shown`, or `fine` once someone answered It's fine, with `fine_by`). It wakes nobody: the agent reads it as the `Check:` line of its next wake.

urn._comment: Room-scoped episode/topic URN forms. Backend: message_format.episode_urn(room, session) / message_format.topic_urn(room). CLI: message_format.room_episode(room) / room_topic(room) with the 'live' session literal. Frontend: mycelium-frontend/src/lib/threads.ts liveEpisodeUrn(room), which is how the channel tells the room's own messages from a thread's. `legacy_episode` is the same room's live episode as a hub before 3.1 recorded it: every reader takes it as `expected_episode`.

envelope._comment: A frozen serialized 'exchange' message content dict. The backend produces this via message_format.envelope_to_dict(message_format.build_envelope(kind=exchange, ...)); the CLI produces the same dict via message_format.build_reply_content(...). The two serializers must agree byte-for-byte or a connector's reply fails the backend persister's parse_envelope. The envelope sits under the `envelope` key; every reader also accepts it under `l9`, the key older records carry (backend and CLI message_format.envelope_of, frontend threads.ts envelopeOf).
